title: Hyland v. Chicago Metro Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC's final vote on the proposed decision was 12–12–0; under the stated rule, Chicago Metro Presbytery's ruling that Hyland's complaint was out of order for lack of standing stands. The proposed panel decision, adopted 2–1, would have answered the issue 'No' and held the complaint judicially out of order because the complainant lacked standing under BCO 43-1; it made no amendments. Concurrences and dissents are recorded.
first_summary: The SJC denied Emily Hyland's complaint against Chicago Metro Presbytery's ruling that her complaint was out of order, holding that she lacked standing under BCO 43-1.
summary: Former church employee Emily Hyland complained to the SJC after Chicago Metro Presbytery ruled her BCO 43 complaint out of order because, as a local-church member, she was not subject to Presbytery's jurisdiction. The SJC was equally divided 12–12–0 on the proposed panel decision, so CMP's ruling stands. That proposed decision would have answered that CMP did not err: Hyland lacked standing to file a BCO 43-1 complaint with Presbytery. No amendments were made. An evenly divided SJC thus leaves the lower ruling in place without a majority rationale.
